question.text: Will at least one additional U.S. state enact a cage-free egg requirement before July 2027?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before July 1, 2027, a U.S. state without an existing cage-free law in effect as of September 1, 2026, enacts a new cage-free requirement.

A cage-free requirement is a law or rule that either bans the use of cages for in-state hens or bans the sale of eggs from non-cage-free hens.
question.fine_print:
To qualify, a cage-free requirement may be enacted by the state legislature, passed by a ballot measure, or implemented via state administrative action. The requirement need not come into effect before July 1, 2027.

If a state legislature passes a cage-free requirement, that will suffice for this question to resolve as Yes, regardless of the action or inaction of the state's governor.

States with cage-free requirement on the books as of September 15, 2026 are Arizona, California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Michigan, Nevada, Oregon, Rhode Island, Utah, and Washington.

# Will another U.S. state enact a cage-free egg requirement before July 2027? Research as of 2026-11-04

I found no new state cage-free law in 2026, and no pending bill that looks close to passing. Since 2025 the movement has been toward rolling laws back, delaying them and fighting them in court.

## 1. Resolution source
- No URL or official data series decides this. It turns on any state enacting a law, passing a ballot measure or adopting an agency rule. The baseline list (as of 2026-09-15) is Arizona, California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Michigan, Nevada, Oregon, Rhode Island, Utah and Washington.
- 2026-11-04: I could not find any newer, authoritative list of state cage-free laws. ASPCA and HSUS do not appear to post updates by date.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened yet that settles the question. I found no new state enacting a cage-free law in 2026.
- 2026-11-02/03: Maricopa County Superior Court Judge Scott Blaney struck down Arizona's agency cage-free rule. He held that the Department of Agriculture lacked specific authority from the legislature and voided the whole rule. The Attorney General is "reviewing" the decision. Humane World for Animals says it may push a future ballot measure. [KJZZ](https://www.kjzz.org/business/2026-11-03/arizona-judge-rules-against-cage-free-requirements-for-egg-producers), [Tucson.com](https://tucson.com/news/state-regional/government-politics/article_c9b5aed0-dbc1-4fea-8cd1-652e2e878fab.html)
- If Arizona later re-enacts the requirement, it is unclear whether that would count. Arizona had a law "in effect" as of September 1, 2026, so it is arguably excluded.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02: The Arizona rule was voided, as above. Before that, Gov. Hobbs had ordered the rule delayed to at least 2034 (March 2025). [KJZZ](https://www.kjzz.org/business/2026-11-03/arizona-judge-rules-against-cage-free-requirements-for-egg-producers)
- 2026-10-07/13: A federal judge (Beckering) dismissed the Justice Department's suit against Michigan's cage-free law for lack of standing, without prejudice. An appeal is expected. A similar Justice Department suit against California was also dismissed. [Michigan Public](https://www.michiganpublic.org/politics-government/2026-10-13/federal-lawsuit-against-michigans-cage-free-egg-law-thrown-out-by-judge)
- 2026-01-30: The Justice Department sued states over cage-free sales laws, citing food costs. [Washington Times](https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/jan/30/eggs-asperated-justice-dept-battles-states-cage-free-laws/). I could not open this page (403 error).
- 2026-01-07: New York's S950 / A652 (a cage-free sales requirement) was re-referred to the Agriculture Committee. That was its last action, and the 2025-26 session ends at the end of 2026, so the bill dies unless it is reintroduced. [NY Senate](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/bills/2025/S950)
- 2025: Maryland's SB 806 / HB 834 (cage-free by 2030) died. HB 834 was dead as of 2025-04-08. I found no 2026 Maryland bill. [MGA](https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/mgawebsite/Legislation/Details/hb0834?ys=2025RS)
- 2025: Other rollbacks:
  - Nevada passed AB 171, allowing the cage-free rule to be suspended during shortages. [8NewsNow](https://www.8newsnow.com/news/politics/nevada-legislature/nevada-legislature-oks-bill-targeting-high-egg-prices-allowing-suspension-of-cage-free-requirement/)
  - A Michigan bill to repeal the state's law was introduced. [CBS](https://www.cbsnews.com/amp/detroit/news/michigan-senator-introduces-bill-repeal-cage-free-egg-law)
  - A Colorado repeal bill failed. [Colorado Politics](https://www.coloradopolitics.com/2025/01/22/republican-efforts-to-repeal-cage-free-egg-law-fails-in-colorado-house-committee/)
- New Jersey: some 2026-27 bills (A5060, A5084, S4499) turned up in searches, but I could not confirm what they cover. [FastDemocracy](https://fastdemocracy.com/bill/nj/2026-2027/bills/NJB00075203/)
- I found no hen-confinement measure on any state ballot on 2026-11-03.

## 4. Base rates
- The existing laws mostly came in one wave:
  - Massachusetts: 2016 ballot measure
  - Rhode Island: 2018
  - California: Prop 12, 2018
  - Michigan, Oregon and Washington: 2019
  - Colorado: 2020
  - Nevada and Utah: 2021
  - Arizona: agency rule, 2022
- That is about 10 states in 2016-2022, roughly 1.5 a year.
- Since 2022, I found no new state law, about 4 years with zero enactments. Bills in New York, New Jersey, Maryland, Illinois (SB 3655, 2023) and Hawaii (Senate passage in 2020) never became law.
- Since 2025, the direction has reversed: suspensions, delays, repeal attempts, the Justice Department suits and the Arizona ruling. Bird flu and egg prices are the main reasons given.
- The window to resolution is about 8 months. It covers most 2027 legislative sessions, which mostly run January to June.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question.
- The Kalshi markets supplied with the question do not match it:
  - "Cage-Free" being mentioned on Cal-Maine's January 6, 2027 earnings call is priced at 0.72. That reflects industry talk about cage-free, not new state laws.
  - The rest (minimum wage, Egg McMuffin price and others) are irrelevant.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- January to June 2027: most state legislative sessions. Candidates are likely Democratic-led states with past bills: New York (new 2027-28 session), New Jersey, Maryland (session ends in April), Illinois, Connecticut, Hawaii and Vermont. I found no announced 2027 bill.
- Possible appeal by the Justice Department in the Michigan and California cases, and a possible appeal by Arizona's Attorney General. These matter for the overall climate rather than directly for resolution.
- Ballot measures: the next regular statewide ballot is November 2027 or 2028, after the deadline. An Arizona measure (floated by Humane World) would probably fall after July 2027, and Arizona may not count anyway.
- Agency rules: Arizona's ruling, which required specific authority from the legislature, may discourage other states from using rules. Utah's law was originally backed by industry, which shows industry-supported laws are possible, but I found nothing similar pending.

If enacted, S950 would ban both in-state cages and sales of non-cage-free eggs, starting 24 months after it becomes law. Nevada passed AB 171 allowing temporary suspension of its cage-free rule, Arizona's governor delayed its rule to 2034, and a Colorado repeal bill failed. [8NewsNow](https://www.8newsnow.com/news/politics/nevada-legislature/nevada-legislature-oks-bill-targeting-high-egg-prices-allowing-suspension-of-cage-free-requirement/), [AWI](https://awionline.org/awi-quarterly/spring-2025/cage-free-laws-in-the-crosshairs/)

## 4. Base rates
- The dates below come from my background knowledge and the Animal Agriculture Alliance (AAA) tracker. Enactments came in clusters: CA 2008 (Prop 2), MA 2016, CA Prop 12 and RI in 2018, WA, OR and MI in 2019, CO 2020, and NV and UT in 2021. Arizona's rule was adopted in roughly 2020-2022. [AAA](https://animalagalliance.org/issues/legislation/)
- No new state has enacted a cage-free law since 2021, almost five years.
- The AAA tracker lists repeated failed cage-free bills: NY (2019, 2023), MD (2023, 2024), ME (2019), NM (2021), NC (2013) and IL (SB 3655, outcome not confirmed). A 2024 Maryland bill "cracked under pressure." forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left and what Yes requires.** About 8 months remain, until July 1, 2027. Yes requires that a state not on the baseline list (Arizona, California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Michigan, Nevada, Oregon, Rhode Island, Utah, Washington) do one of three things:
- its legislature passes a cage-free housing or sales requirement,
- voters approve one by ballot measure, or
- a state agency adopts one by rule.

In practice this means passage during the January to June 2027 legislative sessions. No statewide ballot falls within the window. An Arizona re-enactment likely would not count, since Arizona had a law in effect on September 1, 2026.

**(b) Status quo.** No new state acts, so the question resolves No.

**(c) Base rate.**
- From 2016 to 2022 there was a wave of about 10 states, roughly 1.5 a year.
- From 2023 to 2026 there were zero new enactments in about 4 years, despite bills in New York, New Jersey, Maryland, Illinois and Hawaii.
- Using the recent regime, the chance of at least one enactment in an 8-month window is well under 10%. A Laplace-style estimate from 0 enactments in 4 years gives roughly 10-15% per year, or about 7-10% for 8 months, before adjusting for the current hostile climate.

**(d) Evidence.**

For Yes:
- New York's S950/A652 existed in the 2025-26 session, though it was re-referred to committee on 2026-01-07, which was its last action.
- Some New Jersey bills from 2026-27 (A5060, A5084, S4499) may be relevant, but I could not confirm what they cover.
- Utah shows an industry-backed law is possible.
- Several Democratic-led legislatures convene in 2027.

For No:
- Egg prices and bird flu have shifted momentum toward rollback. Nevada passed AB 171 in 2025, allowing suspension of the rule during shortages, and repeal bills appeared in Michigan and Colorado.
- The DOJ sued states over cage-free laws on 2026-01-30.
- Arizona's governor delayed its rule in 2025, and a court voided the rule on 2026-11-02, which may discourage other states from using agency rules.
- Maryland's 2025 bill died.
- No 2027 bill has been announced, and no measure was on the November 2026 ballot.

**(e) Scenarios.**
- No: The 2027 sessions focus on food affordability, New York and New Jersey bills die in committee, and no agency acts. This is the likely path.
- Yes: Egg prices fall and a newly configured legislature, such as New Jersey under a new governor or New York, quickly passes an HSUS-backed sales requirement before June 2027.

**(f) Adjustment.** I start from about 8% (4 years of zero enactments, short window). I adjust down for the clearly adverse political and legal climate, the absence of any bill with momentum, and the fact that most of the window is a single round of sessions. I stop above 3% because the window includes many legislative sessions and an unexpected passage cannot be ruled out. That gives about 5%.

Probability: 5%

(a) There are about 8 months left (to July 1, 2027), though the listed resolution date is around December 31, 2026. For Yes, a state not on the baseline list (Arizona, California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Michigan, Nevada, Oregon, Rhode Island, Utah, Washington) must enact a cage-free requirement. That can happen by its legislature passing a bill (a governor's signature is not needed), by a ballot measure, or by an agency rule. The rule can either ban cages for in-state hens or ban sales of non-cage-free eggs.

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is No. No new state has enacted a law since 2022, and no pending bill is near passage.

(c) Base rate: there was a wave of about 10 states in 2016-2022, roughly 1.5 per year. Since then there have been about 4 years with zero enactments. Bills in NY, NJ, MD, IL and HI all failed. Using the recent regime, the chance of a new enactment in a given 8-month window is perhaps 5-10%. Adjusting for the reversed trend lowers that.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - Several Democratic-led states (NY, NJ, MD, IL) have recurring bills.
  - Most 2027 legislative sessions fall inside the window.
  - Utah shows an industry-backed law is possible.
- For No:
  - New York's S950 stalled in committee (January 7, 2026) and dies with the session.
  - Maryland's HB 834 died (April 2025), with no 2026 bill.
  - Nevada passed AB 171 allowing suspension (2025).
  - Michigan and Colorado faced repeal attempts (2025).
  - The DOJ sued states over these laws (January 30, 2026).
  - An Arizona judge voided that state's rule (November 2, 2026).
  - Bird flu and egg prices make new mandates politically unattractive.
  - No ballot measures fall before the deadline.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: In 2027, the NY, NJ and MD bills are reintroduced but stay in committee amid egg-price concerns and federal hostility. No ballot measure or agency rule emerges.
- Yes: A Democratic trifecta state such as New Jersey or New York passes a sales ban in its 2027 session, perhaps with a long phase-in and a shortage-suspension clause like Nevada's, possibly backed by producers who have already converted.

(f) I start from about 7% for the recent no-enactment regime. I move down to about 4-5% because the climate is adverse (rollbacks, DOJ suits, the Arizona ruling, egg prices) and no bill is near passage. I keep some tail for an unexpected legislative passage. I don't go below 3% because legislatures can act within 8 months.

Probability: 4%

(a) The question closes on July 1, 2027, about 8 months away, which covers almost all of the 2027 legislative sessions. For Yes, a state that had no cage-free law in effect on September 1, 2026 must enact one before July 1, 2027. That can happen through legislative passage (a governor's veto does not matter), a ballot measure or an agency rule. The law must ban cages for in-state hens or ban the sale of eggs from caged hens. It does not need to take effect before the deadline.

(b) The status quo is No. No new state has enacted a cage-free law since Arizona's rule in 2022, and none is close to passing now.

(c) Base rate: about 10 states enacted laws during the 2016-2022 wave, roughly 1.5 a year. From 2023 to 2026 there were zero enactments in about 4 years. Using the recent regime, and allowing for a small chance that the wave restarts, the chance of at least one enactment in an 8-month window is roughly 5-10%. I weight the recent period more heavily because conditions have changed.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - Several Democratic-led states have had bills before: New York, New Jersey, Maryland, Illinois and Hawaii.
  - New York starts a fresh 2027-28 session.
  - Passage by the legislature alone is enough, which lowers the bar.
  - The DOJ suits against Michigan and California were dismissed for lack of standing in October 2026, which slightly reduces the legal deterrent.
- **For No:**
  - New York's S950 was stuck in committee as of January 2026.
  - Maryland's HB 834 died in April 2025, and I found no 2026 bill.
  - Nevada passed AB 171 in 2025, allowing the cage-free rule to be suspended during shortages.
  - Michigan and Colorado saw repeal attempts in 2025.
  - The DOJ sued states over these laws in January 2026.
  - An Arizona court voided that state's cage-free rule on November 2, 2026.
  - Bird flu and egg-price politics push the other way.
  - No ballot measure can occur before the deadline.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** 2027 sessions focus on budgets and affordability. Cage-free bills in New York and New Jersey get introduced but stall in agriculture committees amid egg-price concerns, and nothing passes by July 1.
- **Yes:** New Jersey's Democratic trifecta, or New York at the end of its session in June, passes a cage-free sales bill. This could be bundled with a phase-in starting in the early 2030s and a suspension clause for shortages, which would make it palatable.

(f) I start at about 7% and move down to 5%. The adverse momentum has been strong since 2025, no announced 2027 bill shows real traction, and the Arizona ruling discourages the agency-rule route. I keep a nonzero tail for legislative surprises and for possible resolution ambiguity, such as a re-enactment in Arizona.

Probability: 5%

(a) About 8 months remain, through June 30, 2027. For Yes, a state without a cage-free law in effect as of September 1, 2026 must enact one. That means passage by its legislature, a ballot measure, or a state administrative rule that either bans cages for in-state hens or bans sales of non-cage-free eggs. Most of the window is the January to June 2027 legislative season. No ballot measure can pass in that period.

(b) Status quo: no new state enacts a cage-free requirement, so the question resolves No. No state has done so since 2021, and nothing was on the November 2026 ballot.

(c) Base rate: from 2016 to 2021 there were about 1 to 3 enactments per year. From 2022 to 2026 there were none in about five comparable legislative seasons. That gives roughly 0 of 5 recent half-year windows, or a base rate of about 5-10% per window. It is lower if weighted to the current climate, where high egg prices from bird flu outbreaks have pushed states to roll back cage-free rules.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - Humane League (2026-05-12) says proposals are "advancing in additional states."
  - New York's S950/A652 exist but stalled in committee (re-referred 2026-01-07).
  - DOJ suits against California (dismissed 2026-03-18) and Michigan (dismissed 2026-10-13) failed, which removes some legal deterrent.
  - Humane World for Animals says it will pursue a legislative or ballot route in Arizona after the court ruling.
- **For No:**
  - The political environment is one of pullback:
    - Nevada passed AB 171 (2025) allowing its rule to be suspended.
    - Arizona's governor delayed its rule to 2034.
    - The Arizona rule was voided by a court (2026-11-02).
    - Repeal bills were filed in Colorado and Michigan.
  - Repeated failures in New York, Maryland, Maine, New Mexico and Illinois.
  - The House farm bill includes the Save Our Bacon Act preemption language, which could return in conference and discourages new laws.
  - Arizona likely wouldn't count, since it is listed as "on the books," and its Republican legislature is hostile in any case.

(e) No scenario: New York's bills are reintroduced in 2027 but die in committee again amid egg-price concerns. Other blue-state bills stall, and Arizona advocates aim for 2028. This is the most likely path.

Yes scenario: New York or New Jersey Democrats move a cage-free bill late in session as egg prices ease, and it passes a chamber vote and the full legislature by June 2027.

(f) I start at about 7% and move down to about 4%. The reasons are the hostile egg-price politics, the absence of any identified bill with momentum, possible federal preemption, and the fact that a 2027 Arizona enactment probably wouldn't count. I keep a small tail because blue-state legislatures can move suddenly and the resolution criteria are somewhat ambiguous.

Probability: 4%

(a) About 8 months remain, until July 1, 2027. Yes requires that a state not on the existing list (realistically NY, NJ, MD, IL, CT, VT, ME, HI or DE) enact a cage-free requirement. That can happen through legislative passage (governor action not needed), administrative rule, or ballot measure. No ballot measure can pass before July 2027, so in practice this means a legislative enactment in the January to June 2027 sessions, or an unlikely agency rule.

(b) Status quo: No. No new state has enacted a cage-free law since 2021 (NV, UT), and no bill is currently near a floor vote.

(c) Base rate: enactments clustered in 2016-2021, with roughly 9 states in 6 years. Since 2021 there have been zero in about 5 legislative seasons, despite repeated bills in NY, MD and others.
